root_cause.text: A race in io_uring ring resizing left io_req_local_work_add()/task-work flag updates using the non-RCU-protected ctx->rings pointer, allowing atomic_or(IORING_SQ_TASKRUN, &ctx->rings->sq_flags) to target an old ring during the swap/free window and cause a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says that with DEFER_TASKRUN | SETUP_TASKRUN, adding task work during resize can OR IORING_SQ_TASKRUN “in the small window of swapping into the new rings and the old rings being freed,” and the fix introduces an RCU-protected ctx->rings_rcu pointer, switches taskrun marking to rcu_dereference(ctx->rings_rcu), and adds synchronize_rcu_expedited() before freeing old rings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an RCU-protected `io_rings` pointer to `io_ring_ctx` to support RCU-based access to ring state.
intent_record.what: A new field, `struct io_rings __rcu *rings_rcu;`, was added to the anonymous inner struct within `struct io_ring_ctx`, before the existing `work_llist`, `retry_llist`, and `check_cq` members.
intent_record.how: This introduces storage for an RCU-protected pointer to `struct io_rings` in the io_uring context, enabling code to reference the rings object through RCU-safe access patterns at runtime; by itself the diff only adds the field and does not change behavior until used elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the RCU-protected rings pointer during ring teardown to prevent stale RCU references to freed ring memory.
intent_record.what: A call to RCU_INIT_POINTER(ctx->rings_rcu, NULL); was added in io_rings_free() immediately after setting ctx->rings = NULL, while the existing cleanup of sq_region, ring_region, and ctx->sq_sqes remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this clears the RCU-protected rings_rcu pointer during ring teardown so RCU readers no longer observe a stale pointer to freed ring memory, preventing use-after-free or invalid access through the RCU path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the RCU-protected rings pointer when allocating SCQ urings so concurrent RCU readers see the correct ring structure.
intent_record.what: A new statement, `rcu_assign_pointer(ctx->rings_rcu, rings);`, was added immediately after assigning `ctx->rings = rings = io_region_get_ptr(&ctx->ring_region);` in `io_allocate_scq_urings()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this initializes the RCU-protected `rings_rcu` pointer to the same ring buffer object as `ctx->rings`, making the ring pointer safely visible to RCU readers and preventing uses of an uninitialized or stale RCU pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ring resize handling by forcing wakeup/taskrun flags on the new SQ ring and updating the RCU rings pointer to the resized ring state.
intent_record.what: The change adds a comment, inserts an atomic_or() call to set IORING_SQ_TASKRUN and IORING_SQ_NEED_WAKEUP in n.rings->sq_flags before replacing ctx->rings, and adds an rcu_assign_pointer() assignment to update ctx->rings_rcu to n.rings after ctx->rings is set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when rings are resized, the new ring's submission queue flags are proactively marked so userspace is forced to react, avoiding missed task-run or wakeup conditions during the transition, and the RCU-visible rings pointer is updated to the new rings so RCU readers see the correct resized ring state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wait for ongoing RCU readers before freeing old ring data during resize to avoid concurrent use-after-free.
intent_record.what: The change adds a comment and a conditional call to synchronize_rcu_expedited() before io_register_free_rings(ctx, to_free), executed only when to_free == &o after releasing completion_lock and mmap_lock in io_register_resize_rings().
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the code is about to free the object referenced by the local old-rings structure (&o), it now waits for any concurrent RCU readers such as io_ctx_mark_taskrun() to finish before freeing it, preventing use-after-free or stale access during ring resize cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an RCU-safe helper to set `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` so userspace notification remains correct during concurrent ring resizing.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `io_ctx_mark_taskrun(struct io_ring_ctx *ctx)` was added. It asserts that the caller is inside an RCU read-side critical section, checks whether `ctx->flags` contains `IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG`, obtains `struct io_rings *rings` via `rcu_dereference(ctx->rings_rcu)`, and sets `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` in `rings->sq_flags` using `atomic_or()`. A comment was also added explaining that this uses the RCU-protected rings pointer to remain safe during concurrent ring resizing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this provides a dedicated, RCU-safe way to mark the shared submission-queue taskrun flag visible to userspace. By dereferencing the rings structure through the RCU-protected pointer instead of assuming a stable direct pointer, it avoids races with concurrent ring resizing while still atomically notifying userspace that task work is pending or required.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor local work enqueueing to use the common `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` helper instead of open-coding SQ taskrun flag updates.
intent_record.what: The change replaces an inline conditional that checked `ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG` and then called `atomic_or(IORING_SQ_TASKRUN, &ctx->rings->sq_flags)` with a single call to `io_ctx_mark_taskrun(ctx)` inside the `if (!head)` block of `io_req_local_work_add()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when local work is added and there is no existing head entry, task-run state marking is now delegated to `io_ctx_mark_taskrun(ctx)` instead of being performed directly in this function. This centralizes the logic for setting the SQ taskrun indicator and may ensure any related conditions or side effects handled by the helper are applied consistently.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document why direct access to ctx->rings is safe here without using rings_rcu in the non-DEFER_TASKRUN case.
intent_record.what: A comment was added immediately before the check of ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG in io_req_normal_work_add(), stating that accessing ctx->rings directly does not need ->rings_rcu because resizing is not supported for the !DEFER_TASKRUN case.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; it documents that the direct use of ctx->rings in this path is considered safe without RCU protection due to the lack of ring resizing support in that configuration.

grouping_result.intent: Add an RCU-protected `io_rings` pointer to `io_ring_ctx` to support RCU-based access to ring state.
Add an RCU-safe helper to set `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` so userspace notification remains correct during concurrent ring resizing.
Refactor local work enqueueing to use the common `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` helper instead of open-coding SQ taskrun flag updates.
Document why direct access to ctx->rings is safe here without using rings_rcu in the non-DEFER_TASKRUN case.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make io_uring ring lifetime, resize, and taskrun notification handling safe for concurrent RCU readers by correctly publishing, updating, and retiring the rings pointer.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is use of the non-RCU-protected ctx->rings during ring resize, leading to stale ring access and UAF. This change adds an RCU-protected io_rings pointer specifically to enable safe RCU-based access to ring state, directly addressing that cause.

The changes directly address the root cause: unsafe concurrent use of the non-RCU-protected ctx->rings pointer during ring resize/teardown. They make rings publication and retirement RCU-safe, update taskrun flag handling to use an RCU-safe path, and ensure old rings are not freed until RCU readers are done, preventing the described use-after-free.

The vulnerability is specifically about unsafe/open-coded SQ taskrun flag updates via ctx->rings during a resize race. Replacing local work enqueueing’s direct flag manipulation with the common io_ctx_mark_taskrun() helper directly affects that vulnerable path and is part of addressing the root cause.
The group directly discusses safety of direct ctx->rings access versus rings_rcu in the task-work flag update path, which is the exact area implicated by the race/use-after-free root cause.

candidates.rationale: This directly dereferences the non-RCU-protected ctx->rings pointer in the taskrun flag update path identified in the root cause, so during ring resize it can target an old ring and cause a use-after-free.
This is the same vulnerable taskrun flag update in another enqueue path, again using ctx->rings without RCU protection while resize can swap and free the old ring.
This unsynchronized publication of the new rings pointer during resize creates the swap window in which concurrent readers using ctx->rings can still race with teardown/free of the old ring.
Freeing the old ring data without first waiting for RCU readers enables the use-after-free when concurrent taskrun flag updates still reference the old ctx->rings.
Directly clearing ctx->rings without RCU-safe pointer handling is part of the unsafe ring lifetime management that leaves stale concurrent users exposed during teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct non-RCU-protected dereference of ctx->rings in the task-work flag update path described by the root cause. During ring resizing, ctx->rings can be swapped and the old ring freed concurrently, so this atomic_or() can target stale freed ring memory and trigger the use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7642e668606009fcd3fe1fc161a79ef90403d507
Author: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Date:   Thu Jan 22 08:55:45 2026 -0700

    io_uring: split out task work code into tw.c
    
    Move the task work handling code out of io_uring.c into a new tw.c file.
    This includes the local work, normal work, and fallback work handling
    infrastructure.
    
    The associated tw.h header contains io_should_terminate_tw() as a static
    inline helper, along with the necessary function declarations.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly shows the task-work flag updates that use `ctx->rings->sq_flags` without any RCU-protected access to `ctx->rings`, which matches the stated root cause. In `io_req_local_work_add()`, when `!head`, the code does `atomic_or(IORING_SQ_TASKRUN, &ctx->rings->sq_flags);`. There is a `guard(rcu)();` earlier in the function, but that protects the local work list traversal/comments around `work_llist` and `first_req`; there is no RCU dereference or protected load of `ctx->rings` before taking `&ctx->rings->sq_flags`. The vulnerable construct is therefore present. The same direct pattern also appears elsewhere in this file, e.g. `io_req_normal_work_add()`, `io_run_local_work_continue()`, `__io_run_local_work()` and `ctx_flush_and_put()` using `atomic_or/atomic_andnot(..., &ctx->rings->sq_flags)`. Since the root cause is specifically that task-work flag updates use the non-RCU-protected `ctx->rings` pointer during ring resize/swap, and this code still does exactly that, the fix is not present.
